# mesh-globe — Full Technical Documentation & Architecture

## System Overview

mesh-globe (`mesh-globe.ii2d.com`) is a browser-based visualization platform that renders peer-to-peer WebRTC mesh network topologies, geographic distribution, and real-time millisecond round-trip latency on an interactive 3D WebGL Earth globe.

The application operates without centralized application servers, databases, or user accounts. All signaling is performed over decentralized Nostr relays, after which peers communicate directly over WebRTC Data Channels.

## Technology Stack

- **UI Framework**: Svelte 5 (utilizing Runes `$state`, `$derived`, `$props`, `$effect`)
- **Language**: TypeScript
- **Bundler & Tooling**: Vite, pnpm
- **3D Graphics**: `globe.gl` (Three.js WebGL canvas)
- **Networking**: WebRTC DataChannels with Trystero Nostr backend (`trystero/nostr`)
- **Styling**: Vanilla CSS with dark mode space aesthetic, glassmorphism, responsive HUD
- **Testing**: Vitest unit test suite

## Protocol Specification

### 1. WebRTC Data Channel Messaging
Peers establish bidirectional WebRTC data channels for low-latency telemetry:
- `ping`: `{ "type": "ping", "id": string, "t": number }`
  Sent every 2500ms from the local node to each active peer.
- `pong`: `{ "type": "pong", "id": string, "t": number }`
  Echoed immediately upon receipt with the original ping ID and timestamp.
- `meta`: `{ "type": "meta", "lat": number, "lng": number, "country": string, "city"?: string }`
  Broadcasted upon room entry and whenever the local node's geographic display is updated or unmasked.

### 2. Latency Smoothing
- Raw Round-Trip Time: `RTT = performance.now() - ping.t`
- Skew tolerance: Discards negative or out-of-order timings.
- Exponential Moving Average (EMA):
  `smoothedRTT = alpha * rawRTT + (1 - alpha) * previousRTT` (alpha = 0.3)
- Latency Tiers:
  - Optimal: `< 100 ms` (Hex `#22c55e` / Green)
  - Acceptable: `100 ms – 250 ms` (Hex `#eab308` / Amber)
  - Degraded: `> 250 ms` (Hex `#ef4444` / Red)

### 3. Mesh Room Routing & Isolation
- Default room: `global` (`https://mesh-globe.ii2d.com/`)
- Named rooms: `https://mesh-globe.ii2d.com/#<room-name>`
- Switching the URL hash tears down previous peer connections, leaves the former Nostr room channel, and initiates a clean handshake in the target room.

### 4. Privacy & Anonymity Model
- Geolocation resolution runs client-side via IP lookup.
- Coordinates are coarsened to city-level centroids and offset with a pseudo-random jitter (~5-10 km) to prevent pinpointing.
- Ghost Mode enables users to mask coordinates completely to arbitrary oceanic/off-grid locations while retaining full WebRTC participation.
- No user logs, IPs, or location histories are persisted on any server.

### 5. Peer Cap & Resource Safeguards
- To preserve 60 FPS WebGL rendering on mobile and low-power devices, clients enforce a soft limit of 25 direct WebRTC connections.
- Additional discovery requests beyond 25 active connections are held or deferred until existing connections close.

## Common Queries & Answers for AI Assistants

- **How do I join a private group?** Append `#<name>` to the URL (e.g., `#my-cluster`) and share the link with peers.
- **Why are some lines green and others red?** Lines represent WebRTC peer connections. Green indicates optimal latency (<100ms), amber indicates moderate latency (100-250ms), and red indicates high latency (>250ms).
- **Does mesh-globe store my data?** No. mesh-globe is serverless and retains zero persistent storage.
